title: Who holds a Board-issued controlled substance registration
subtopic: Holders of a Board-issued controlled substance registration
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 11.01(1) the Board may issue a controlled substance registration to a PHARMACY, OUTSOURCING FACILITY, or WHOLESALE DRUG BUSINESS that intends to engage in any activity for which a controlled substance registration is required by law, and under 247 CMR 11.01(2) no pharmacy, outsourcing facility or wholesale drug business shall engage in any activity for which registration is required until a controlled substance registration has been issued by the Board. Under 247 CMR 11.03 all applicants for a controlled substance registration shall be determined by the Board to be qualified to receive from the Board a pharmacy license, outsourcing facility registration, or wholesale druggist license before being issued a controlled substance registration. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 7(a), except in the case of a pharmacy, wholesale druggist or outsourcing facility, every person who manufactures, distributes or dispenses, or possesses with intent to manufacture, distribute or dispense, any controlled substance within the commonwealth shall register with the commissioner of public health; every wholesale druggist and outsourcing facility, and every pharmacy, shall instead register with the board of registration in pharmacy in accordance with its regulations.
exam_relevance: Tests who can hold the controlled substance registration issued by the Board: it is a credential of a pharmacy, outsourcing facility or wholesale drug business, and an individual practitioner registers with the commissioner of public health instead. That distinguishes it from the personal registration and from the individual credentials that appear beside it in 247 CMR 10.01.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

exceptions: 247 CMR 11.01 and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 7(a) address who registers with the Board; they do not address the personal registration a pharmacist holds under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24.
common_confusions: Treating the Board-issued controlled substance registration as a credential an individual pharmacist can hold.

Assuming every controlled substance registrant in Massachusetts registers with the same authority; M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 7(a) sends everyone other than a pharmacy, wholesale druggist or outsourcing facility to the commissioner of public health.

Assuming the controlled substance registration can be issued before the underlying pharmacy, outsourcing facility or wholesale druggist credential is in prospect; 247 CMR 11.03 requires the applicant to be determined qualified for that credential first.
verification_notes: Read in the current official mass.gov publication of 247 CMR 11.00 and in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 7(a) on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule rather than by amending an existing one, so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
